prompt: Assess this claim: Indigenous people have lower average life expectancy than the national average.

settings.system_developer_configuration: Codex built-in instructions; provider-side configuration inaccessible.
settings.developer_instructions: Respond directly to the user's proposition. Do not use tools, inspect files, search the web, or ask follow-up questions.
limitations: CLI does not expose an inference seed.
Model alias and provider instructions may change.
Results apply to this purposive corpus and selected interface only.

exact_response:
The claim is **often supported, but needs a country and time period to be assessed precisely**. In countries such as Australia, Canada, and New Zealand, Indigenous populations have generally had lower average life expectancy than the overall national population.

The size of the gap varies across Indigenous peoples, regions, and years. Estimates can also be affected by incomplete identification in health and mortality records.

These disparities reflect factors such as colonisation, socioeconomic disadvantage, discrimination, and unequal access to healthcare; they do not establish an inherent biological difference. A more precise claim would specify the population, country, period, and data source.
